questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 10 days. The ulcer has clean, indurated margins and a smooth base. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spiral organisms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) presents as a painless, indurated ulcer with clean margins caused by Treponema pallidum, demonstrated by dark-field microscopy showing corkscrew motility.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with erythematous plaques with silvery-white scales on knees, elbows, and scalp. Auspitz sign is positive. Histopathology shows parakeratosis, Munro microabscesses, and suprapapillary thinning. What is the primary pathological mechanism?
questions.exp: Psoriasis is driven by Th1/Th17 T-cell mediated immune activation causing keratinocyte hyperproliferation (epidermal turnover reduced from 28 days to 3-4 days), resulting in parakeratosis and Munro microabscesses.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman develops tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin, predominantly on the trunk and flexures. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposits at the dermoepidermal junction. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae (subepidermal), negative Nikolsky sign, and linear IgG/C3 deposits at DEJ on DIF. Autoantibodies target BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230 in hemidesmosomes.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden painful erythematous nodules over the face and limbs with fever, malaise, and iritis. Nerve tenderness is absent. What is this reaction and the most appropriate immediate treatment?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 reaction) occurs in BL/LL leprosy due to immune complex deposition. Thalidomide (100-400mg/day) is the drug of choice; prednisolone is used for systemic involvement or when thalidomide is contraindicated.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman presents with scaly, non-itchy macules on the trunk that fluoresce yellow-green under Wood's lamp. KOH mount shows short hyphae and clusters of round spores ('spaghetti and meatballs' appearance). What organism is responsible?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (lipophilic yeast). KOH shows the classic 'spaghetti and meatballs' (short hyphae + spores) pattern. Wood's lamp shows yellow-green fluorescence.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with a pearly, telangiectatic papule on the nose with rolled borders that has been slowly enlarging for 2 years. Histology shows peripheral palisading of basaloid cells with retraction artifact. What is the treatment of choice for a lesion <2 cm on the nose?
opts: Wide local excision with 1 cm margins
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma on the nose (high-risk area, H-zone) requires Mohs micrographic surgery for the highest cure rate and tissue conservation. Mohs offers 99% cure rate for primary BCC on facial sites.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman with SLE develops a photosensitive butterfly-shaped rash, alopecia, and oral ulcers. ANA is positive (1:640, homogeneous pattern). Anti-dsDNA antibodies are markedly elevated. Which serological marker best correlates with disease activity and nephritis?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibodies are highly specific for SLE and their titers correlate with disease activity, particularly lupus nephritis. They participate in immune complex formation and glomerular deposition.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child has grouped vesicles on an erythematous base around the mouth and nose, with honey-colored crusting. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. What is the first-line topical treatment?
questions.exp: Impetigo contagiosa (non-bullous) is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Topical mupirocin (2%) is the first-line treatment as it has excellent activity against S. aureus including MRSA.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with grouped vesicles on the sacral area recurring every month, preceded by tingling. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells with intranuclear inclusions. The most appropriate antiviral for suppressive therapy is:
questions.exp: Herpes simplex virus type 2 (genital herpes) suppressive therapy: Valacyclovir 500mg once daily is preferred for its better bioavailability (55% vs 10-20% for acyclovir) and once-daily dosing improving compliance.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with borderline tuberculoid leprosy develops acute swelling of the face, new skin lesions, and severe nerve tenderness in the ulnar nerve with sudden onset of wrist drop. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Increase clofazimine dose and continue MDT
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction with acute neuritis and nerve function impairment requires immediate corticosteroids (prednisolone 40mg/day, tapering over 6 months) to prevent permanent nerve damage. MDT must be continued.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman develops flaccid bullae on the oral mucosa and skin. Bullae rupture easily leaving painful erosions. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits in epidermis (chicken wire pattern). The target antigen is:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris: autoantibodies target desmoglein-3 (mucosal disease) and desmoglein-1 (skin involvement). DIF shows intercellular IgG in a fish-net/chicken-wire pattern throughout the epidermis.

questions.q: A 16-year-old athlete presents with itchy annular plaques with central clearing and raised scaly margins on the groin and inner thighs. KOH preparation is positive. Which organism is the most common cause of tinea cruris?
questions.exp: Tinea cruris is most commonly caused by Epidermophyton floccosum, which uniquely lacks microconidia and produces only macroconidia. Trichophyton rubrum is also common but E. floccosum predominates in groin infections.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with a painless, progressive ulcer on the genitalia with beefy-red granulation tissue and raised margins. Donovan bodies are seen on tissue smear (Wright-Giemsa stain). What is the first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Granuloma inguinale (Donovanosis) caused by Klebsiella granulomatis. WHO guidelines recommend azithromycin 1g weekly (or 500mg daily) for minimum 3 weeks as first-line, continued until lesions heal completely.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis develops sclerodactyly, Raynaud's phenomenon, calcinosis cutis, telangiectasia, and dysphagia. ANA shows anticentromere pattern. This presentation is best classified as:
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) represents limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis. Anti-centromere antibodies are highly specific for this variant.

questions.q: A 70-year-old farmer presents with a 3cm warty plaque on the dorsum of hand with irregular borders, induration, and ulceration. Histology shows atypical keratinocytes with keratin pearls invading the dermis. Perineural invasion is noted. What is the most important prognostic factor for recurrence?
questions.exp: In cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, perineural invasion is a high-risk feature associated with highest recurrence rates (>15%) and metastatic potential. It requires Mohs surgery and consideration of adjuvant radiotherapy.

questions.q: During a patch test procedure, reactions are read at 48 hours and 96 hours. A patient shows a reaction at 96 hours that was absent at 48 hours. This is most likely:
questions.exp: In patch testing, reactions appearing at D4/D7 that were negative at D2 represent late-positive reactions, seen with corticosteroids, neomycin, and some metals. This indicates Type IV (delayed) hypersensitivity.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with comedones, papules, and pustules on the face. Which topical agent primarily targets comedone formation (comedolytic) and is also anti-inflammatory?
questions.exp: Tretinoin (all-trans retinoic acid) is the most potent comedolytic agent - it normalizes follicular keratinization and has anti-inflammatory effects. It is the gold standard for comedonal acne.

questions.q: A 26-year-old woman presents with pruritic vesicles over the elbows, knees, and buttocks symmetrically. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at the tips of dermal papillae. Duodenal biopsy shows villous atrophy. The primary treatment is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis is associated with celiac disease. Granular IgA at dermal papillae tips on DIF is pathognomonic. Treatment: strict gluten-free diet (disease-modifying) + dapsone (symptomatic relief).

questions.q: A 45-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 50 cells/uL) develops painful grouped vesicles along the T5 dermatome that coalesce into hemorrhagic bullae. Appropriate antiviral therapy is:
opts: IV acyclovir 10mg/kg every 8 hours for 7-10 days
Oral valacyclovir 500mg twice daily for 5 days
questions.exp: Severe herpes zoster in immunocompromised patients (HIV with CD4 <100) with disseminated or hemorrhagic lesions requires IV acyclovir 10mg/kg every 8 hours for 7-10 days to prevent visceral dissemination.

questions.q: A newborn presents at birth with a collodion-like membrane covering the entire body. By 2 weeks, the membrane sheds revealing generalized ichthyosis. Genetic analysis shows transglutaminase-1 (TGM1) mutation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lamellar ichthyosis (autosomal recessive) most commonly results from TGM1 mutations. Presents as collodion baby, evolving to generalized large plate-like scales. Non-bullous, non-erythrodermic variant.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman with dermatomyositis develops heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules, and proximal muscle weakness. Anti-MDA5 antibody is positive. What complication should be actively screened for in this patient?
questions.exp: Anti-MDA5 (anti-CADM-140) antibodies in dermatomyositis are strongly associated with clinically amyopathic DM and rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD), which carries high mortality and requires urgent treatment.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man presents with itchy red-brown plaques on the lower legs with superficial erosions and crusting. Biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia with dyskeratosis, pleomorphism, and mitotic figures, but an intact basement membrane. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bowen's disease (SCC in situ) presents as a well-demarcated erythematous scaly plaque. Histology shows full-thickness epidermal dysplasia with dyskeratosis, pleomorphism, and intact basement membrane.

questions.q: A 42-year-old man presents with nodular thickening of ear lobes and eyebrows, diffuse shiny skin, and inability to wrinkle the forehead. Slit skin smear shows a Bacterial Index (BI) of 4+ with solid stained bacilli. What MDT regimen is prescribed?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy with BI 4+ is multibacillary (MB) leprosy. WHO MB-MDT: rifampicin 600mg monthly (supervised) + clofazimine 300mg monthly + 50mg daily + dapsone 100mg daily for 12 months.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman undergoes liquid nitrogen cryotherapy for a wart. The mechanism of tissue destruction in cryotherapy is:
opts: Ice crystal formation causing intracellular damage and vascular stasis
questions.exp: Cryotherapy destroys tissue through: (1) intracellular ice crystal formation rupturing cell membranes, (2) osmotic damage during thaw, and (3) vascular stasis causing ischemic necrosis. Rapid freezing and slow thawing maximize cell death.

questions.q: A patient on long-term dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops pallor and breathlessness. CBC shows hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL with Heinz bodies on peripheral smear. G6PD level is normal. What is the most likely mechanism?
questions.exp: Dapsone causes dose-dependent hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia through oxidative stress, even in G6PD-normal patients. Heinz bodies represent denatured hemoglobin. This is an expected pharmacological effect, not an idiosyncratic reaction.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman with recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis, and erythema nodosum presents to the clinic. Pathergy test is positive. HLA-B51 association is confirmed. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease (ISG criteria): recurrent oral ulcers + 2 of (genital ulcers, ocular involvement, skin lesions, positive pathergy test). HLA-B51 is associated. Pathergy test (prick with needle -> pustule >2mm at 48h) is characteristic.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with asymptomatic hypopigmented macules on the face since childhood that do not tan on sun exposure. Wood's lamp shows ivory-white fluorescence with indistinct margins. Dermoscopy reveals retained perifollicular pigmentation. What is the diagnosis?
opts: Ash leaf macule of tuberous sclerosis
questions.exp: Nevus depigmentosus (achromic nevus): congenital, segmental hypopigmented macule with stable borders. On Wood's lamp, it appears ivory-white (not chalk-white as in vitiligo). Dermoscopy shows retained perifollicular pigmentation unlike vitiligo.

questions.q: An 8-year-old child presents with severe eczema, recurrent cold Staphylococcal abscesses, pneumonia with pneumatoceles, and markedly elevated serum IgE (>2000 IU/mL) with eosinophilia. STAT3 loss-of-function mutation is found. What is this syndrome?
questions.exp: Hyper-IgE syndrome (Job's syndrome): STAT3 mutation causing impaired Th17 differentiation -> cold staphylococcal abscesses, eczema, recurrent pneumonia with pneumatoceles, skeletal anomalies, characteristic facies, and markedly elevated IgE.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man with psoriasis is started on methotrexate. After 6 months, the most reliable non-invasive way to monitor for hepatic fibrosis is:
opts: Serial liver function tests every 3 months
Liver biopsy after cumulative dose of 3.5-4g
questions.exp: P3NP (procollagen III N-terminal peptide) is a serum marker of hepatic fibrosis used in UK/European guidelines as an alternative to routine liver biopsy in MTX-treated psoriasis patients. It is elevated with active hepatic fibrosis.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with painful inguinal lymphadenopathy (buboes) with 'groove sign'. A small painless genital ulcer healed spontaneously 2 weeks ago. Complement fixation test titer is 1:256. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) caused by C. trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3. Classic presentation: transient painless papule -> tender inguinal lymphadenopathy with groove sign (Greenblatt's sign). CFT titer >1:64 is diagnostic. Treatment: doxycycline 100mg BD for 21 days.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with a pigmented lesion on the sole showing asymmetry, irregular borders, variegated color (black, brown, grey areas), and diameter 12mm. Dermoscopy shows irregular pigment network, regression structures, and blue-white veil. What is the next best step?
opts: Observe for 3 months and repeat dermoscopy
Excisional biopsy with 1-2mm margins for histology
Punch biopsy of darkest area only
questions.exp: Acral lentiginous melanoma (most common melanoma in Asians/Africans) presents with ABCDE features on acral sites. Excisional biopsy with narrow margins (1-2mm) is the gold standard for diagnosis before definitive treatment planning.
